misconceptions.description: Keeping a plan unchanged because the design is sound in principle despite field data showing it failed
misconceptions.trigger: candidate defends the original plan or adds penalties instead of addressing the observed barrier
misconceptions.feedback: Let the field data drive the change. If most students hit a barrier, revise the plan toward that barrier.

misconceptions.description: Scrapping an entire plan after one rough lesson without isolating what actually failed
misconceptions.trigger: candidate discards working and failing components together based on one session
misconceptions.feedback: Separate the part that failed from the part that worked, then revise only the cause.

misconceptions.description: Adopting an AI revision that reframes an access problem as an engagement problem
misconceptions.trigger: candidate follows an AI suggestion that ignores the cause she observed
misconceptions.feedback: When AI reframes the cause, hold to your field evidence and revise toward the barrier you actually observed.

misconceptions.description: Treating a sense that the next lesson felt better as proof the revision worked
misconceptions.trigger: candidate records an impression instead of follow-up data
misconceptions.feedback: Show the original plan, the prompting data, the change, and follow-up data on whether participation rose.
